guards.verdict: DEFECTIVE in three places — three whole features had only one-sided assertions behind them; repaired additively and re-falsified three ways
guards.note: Lesson 1 three times over in one file. Block [8] is headed 'the global Smooth slider is convergent' and its finite / bounded / never-INFLATES trio are all satisfied by a slider that does nothing. Block [3] deliberately skips the 'actually deformed' check for the corrective brushes (correct on a flat mesh, where they ARE no-ops) and [3b] then covered only `restore`, so `smooth` fell through the gap between them. Block [7] is headed 'Catmull-Rom render upsampling' and every one of its four assertions — S=1 identity, control-point pass-through, finiteness, flat-grid interior uniformity — is also satisfied by linear interpolation, because Catmull-Rom's distinguishing property is what it does BETWEEN the control points and nothing sampled there.
guards.measurement: Instrumented with a throwaway probe in the gitignored debug/scratch/ before choosing any bound. smoothAll over 400 frames at strength 1: deviation 41.75 -> 15.96 (ratio 0.382 vs the 0.9 bound, 2.4x margin), max vertex move 0.290 (29x margin on 0.01). smooth brush on a deliberately creased mesh: roughness 1.526 -> 0.898 (ratio 0.589 vs 0.9), max move 0.0564. Cubic-vs-linear deviation, restricted to cells whose full 4-point stencil is interior: warped 0.003912 (3.9x the 1e-3 floor), flat 1.0e-8 (100x under the 1e-6 ceiling). The interior restriction is load-bearing and was itself measured — the clamp-extended BOUNDARY cells do not reproduce linears (0.0106 there), so a whole-grid version of that check would have been wrong in the other direction.

guards.inputsVanishCheck: THE FINDING. Both halves derive their workload from live registries and a workload that never ran produces zero issues and zero rows. Dropping the harness's `import '../engine-gmt/formulas/index'` side effect took the registry 55 -> 7: the READER correctly went RED on snapshot drift, and then the WRITER truncated the tracked baseline to ZERO BYTES, printed 'snapshot: 0 disabled compat rows', and exited 0 — after which the reader printed 'snapshot matches' and exited 0 forever, on an empty file. The harness's own red-run message ('run with --write to update the baseline if the drift is intentional') routes you straight into that.
